source.title: Open Problem: Average-Case Hardness of Hypergraphic Planted Clique Detection

accepted.question_text: For hypergraphic planted clique detection, let a d-hypergraph be an order-d extension of a graph, let G_d(N, 1/2) be the Erdos-Renyi d-hypergraph on N vertices with each d-vertex hyperedge independently present with probability 1/2, and let G_d(N, 1/2, kappa) be the model obtained by choosing kappa vertices uniformly at random and adding every hyperedge whose vertices all lie in that planted set. Given the adjacency tensor A of the observed hypergraph, what is the sharp threshold for the planted clique size kappa that guarantees that HPC can be solved by singular value decomposition after matricizing or unfolding A, and is there another polynomial-time algorithm for HPC that succeeds below that SVD threshold?

evidence.quote: Can we establish the sharp limit of κ

accepted.question_text: For the hypergraphic planted clique detection problem G_d(N, 1/2) versus G_d(N, 1/2, kappa), where a test solves detection when the sum of type-I and type-II errors converges to zero, can the conjectured polynomial-time hardness of HPC detection below the kappa on the order of sqrt(N) regime be supported for additional classes of algorithms, specifically statistical query algorithms, sum-of-squares algorithms, belief propagation, approximate message passing, or other algorithmic models beyond the already cited evidence from Metropolis algorithms and low-degree polynomial algorithms?

evidence.quote: more evidence for HPC detection conjecture under more classes

accepted.question_text: At the threshold kappa = O(N^(1/2 - tau)) for tau > 0, what is the precise computational-hardness relationship between hypergraphic planted clique detection and ordinary planted clique detection? Because fixing d - 2 indices of the adjacency tensor of a d-hypergraph and varying the remaining two gives an adjacency matrix corresponding to a planted clique detection problem, HPC detection is no harder than PC detection; is HPC strictly easier than PC detection, or can one prove a randomized polynomial-time reduction from PC detection to HPC detection showing that the two detection problems are equivalently hard at this threshold?
accepted.context_brief: Equivalence of HPC and PC detection

evidence.quote: what is relationship between HPC detection and PC detection

Mapped title and abstract, Section 1 Introduction, Section 2 Planted Clique Detection and Hypergraphic Planted Clique Detection, Section 3 How hard is HPC detection?, and references. Section 2 supplies the HPC and PC definitions; Section 3 contains the explicit challenge blocks.

Expanded Challenge 3 with the threshold kappa = O(N^(1/2 - tau)), the tensor-to-matrix reduction showing HPC is no harder than PC, and the unresolved reverse reduction from PC to HPC.
